what_happened: The job asked to keep read requests in the plan and drain queue, and to fix the plan room check. It was rejected. The verifier failed 1 of 9 acceptance criteria: "cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check pass." There was one major finding: behavior criterion 7 was unmet because its evidence did not cite commands that actually ran (D43). No failed checks are listed. The queue change itself may be correct. The verifier could not accept the claim that the test, clippy and fmt commands passed, because the record gave no evidence of running them.
cause: Nothing in the build requires each criterion to have recorded evidence, in the form the verifier demands (commands that ran, with their output), before handover. The build step can finish with the cargo test, clippy and fmt gate unrecorded or unrun. The verifier then finds the gap only at the final verdict, where rejection is the only outcome. This is the same pattern as the other final-verification misses. The earlier job in this family (y9dy) also touched the same drain and plan code, and its rejection did not lead to any pre-handover check of evidence. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the evidence text, the cargo output or whether the commands were run.
prevention: Add a pre-handover code check that runs before the job is sent to the verifier. For every acceptance criterion that names a command (cargo test, clippy, fmt --check, or a CLI behavior), the check requires an evidence entry that records the exact command, its exit status and its output tail, produced by Athena running the command in the final snapshot. If any entry is missing, or was recorded before the last edit, the job goes back to the build instead of to the verifier. This catches the whole class of criteria that are unmet only because the evidence is missing.
proposed_request: Before a job is handed to the verifier, add a check that every acceptance criterion naming a command (such as cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo fmt --check, or a CLI behavior run) has recorded evidence. The evidence must give the exact command, its exit status and the tail of its output, and it must come from a run against the final state of the work. If any such evidence is missing or is older than the last change to the work, the job must go back to the build with a message naming the criteria concerned. It must not go to the verifier. Add tests showing that: a job with all evidence present passes the check; a job with a missing command record is sent back; a job whose evidence predates a later edit is sent back. Make sure cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check pass, and cite the commands that ran in the evidence (D43).
